correctness.rationale: The path basis makes independent length-two equations with free radical-square coefficients. Each arrow pair labels a zero vector or a projective line; determinant zero equates adjacent lines, while anticommutator zero alternates the sign involution. Connected nonbipartite components force one of exactly two fixed lines in odd characteristic. The support-sum identities, bipartite sign-switch isomorphism, strict positivity, and seven-arrow acyclic witness follow. Standalone direct finite checks passed in 22 configurations including GF(4); finite checks supplement but do not replace the all-quiver proof.

The odd-transition graph criterion has a constructive linear-equivalence proof and a nontrivial acyclic seven-arrow counterexample to the naive directed-cycle criterion.
